turns.prompt:
You are given an attached CSV file b3_supercon_data.csv: 300 real samples,
column `composition` (element fractions as a compact formula string) and
column `target` (the measured critical temperature Tc (K)).

Propose a composition — a value for each element fraction below, within each
observed range, that MAXIMIZES critical temperature Tc (K) AND stays robust
— its critical temperature Tc (K) must not collapse under a ±5% change in
any single variable (seek a broad optimum, not a sharp peak). Design
variables:
  - O (fraction in [0, 0.697674])
  - Cu (fraction in [0, 0.454545])
  - Ba (fraction in [0, 0.333333])
  - Sr (fraction in [0, 0.285714])
  - Y (fraction in [0, 0.4])
  - Ca (fraction in [0, 0.272727])
  - La (fraction in [0, 0.78])
  - Bi (fraction in [0, 0.521978])
  - Fe (fraction in [0, 0.502513])
  - Nb (fraction in [0, 0.98])
  - C (fraction in [0, 0.972])
  - Pr (fraction in [0, 0.265043])
  - As (fraction in [0, 0.5])
  - B (fraction in [0, 1])
  - Pb (fraction in [0, 0.5])
  - Ce (fraction in [0, 0.28])
  - Mo (fraction in [0, 1])
  - V (fraction in [0, 0.9918])
  - Zn (fraction in [0, 1])
  - Ni (fraction in [0, 0.6])

Reason from the training data, then end with your explicit proposal, e.g.
"Final: O=0.348837, Cu=0.227273, Ba=0.166667, Sr=0.142857, Y=0.2,
Ca=0.136364, La=0.39, Bi=0.260989, Fe=0.251256, Nb=0.49, C=0.486,

turns.answer_text:
The highest measured Tc values in the supplied data belong to the cuprate family. After discarding samples whose constitutive elements fall outside the 20 allowed design variables (Hg, Tl, H, S, \ldots), the remaining high-Tc points cluster around two closely related 1223-type stoichiometries:

- HgBa2Ca2Cu3O8 (Tc = 132 K)  
- Ba2Ca2Cu3O (Tc = 126 K)

Both map onto atomic fractions that lie comfortably inside the observed ranges (O \(\approx\) 0.53, Cu \(\approx\) 0.20, Ba \(\approx\) 0.13, Ca \(\approx\) 0.13).  The same region of composition space also contains the well-sampled Bi-2223 and Y-123 families (Tc = 90–110 K), demonstrating that Tc remains high under modest stoichiometric perturbations.  Consequently a point that realises the 1223 cation ratios while setting every non-essential element identically to zero is simultaneously a high-value and a broad optimum: a \(\pm\)5 % relative change in any single coordinate stays inside the experimentally documented high-Tc plateau and cannot introduce the known Tc-suppressing substituents (Zn, Ni, Fe, Pr, \ldots).
